title: Ecosystem
syllabus: Ecosystem - Patterns, components; Productivity (GPP, NPP, Secondary productivity) and Decomposition (Fragmentation, Leaching, Catabolism, Humification, Mineralisation); Energy flow (PAR, 10% law, food chains, food webs); Ecological pyramids - Pyramids of number, biomass, and energy.

questions.question: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an ecosystem (e.g., trees occupying top vertical strata, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses the bottom layers) is called:
questions.solution: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification. For example, in a forest ecosystem, trees occupy the top vertical strata or layer, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

questions.question: The four basic functional aspects of an ecosystem that work together as a unified unit are:
options: Productivity, Decomposition, Energy flow, and Nutrient cycling
Stratification, Speciation, Food chain, and Ecological succession
questions.solution: The four functional aspects that are essential to understand the working of an ecosystem are: (1) Productivity, (2) Decomposition, (3) Energy flow, and (4) Nutrient cycling.

questions.question: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is mathematically related to Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) and Respiration loss ($R$) as:
questions.solution: Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilized by plants in respiration ($R$). Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses ($R$) is the Net Primary Productivity (NPP): $\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R$.

questions.question: The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Despite occupying about 70 percent of the Earth's surface, the oceans contribute only about:
questions.solution: The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the Earth's surface, the productivity of the oceans is only 55 billion tons; the rest (115 billion tons) is from land ecosystems due to high terrestrial nutrient availability and light.

questions.question: Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of:
options: Formation of new organic matter by consumers (heterotrophs)
Total biomass synthesized by autotrophs per unit time
Energy lost as heat during cellular respiration
Decomposition of organic matter by saprophytes
questions.solution: Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers (herbivores, carnivores) from the ingested primary biomass.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the five sequential steps of the decomposition process:

List-I (Step of Decomposition)List-II (Process / Defining Characteristic)
(A) Fragmentation(I) Water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and precipitate as unavailable salts
(B) Leaching(II) Breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by detritivores (e.g., Earthworm)
(C) Catabolism(III) Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances
(D) Humification(IV) Accumulation of dark-colored, amorphous, colloidal organic substance highly resistant to microbial action
(E) Mineralisation(V) Release of inorganic nutrients by degradation of humus by specific microbes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Fragmentation: Detritivores break detritus into smaller particles; Leaching: Water-soluble inorganic nutrients sink into soil horizons; Catabolism: Microbial enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances; Humification: Leads to dark amorphous humus; Mineralisation: Microbes release inorganic nutrients from humus.

questions.question: Humus is an extremely valuable component of soil because it:
options: Is dark, amorphous, colloidal, highly resistant to microbial action, decomposes extremely slowly, and serves as a reservoir of nutrients
Is light-colored, highly soluble in water, and decomposes in minutes
Is formed only under extreme anaerobic freezing conditions
Consists solely of pure crystalline minerals without organic matter
questions.solution: Humification leads to the accumulation of a dark-coloured amorphous substance called humus that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Being colloidal in nature, it serves as a reservoir of nutrients.

questions.question: Decomposition rate is slower if the detritus is rich in ________, whereas it is much quicker if the detritus is rich in ________:
options: Lignin and Chitin; Nitrogen and water-soluble substances (like sugars)
Nitrogen and Sugars; Lignin and Suberin
questions.solution: Chemical quality of detritus determines decomposition velocity: decomposition rate is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker if detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars.

questions.question: Which of the following environmental conditions favors the FASTEST rate of decomposition in an ecosystem?
options: Warm temperature and moist environment with abundant aeration
Extreme desert heat and zero moisture
questions.solution: Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes. Warm and moist environment favors decomposition, whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition, resulting in buildup of organic materials.

questions.question: Of the total incident solar radiation reaching the Earth's atmosphere, what percentage constitutes Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR)?
questions.solution: Of the incident solar radiation that reaches the Earth, less than 50 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR, spanning wavelengths 400–700 nm).

questions.question: Plants and photosynthetic autotrophs capture what percentage of the Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) to sustain the entire living world?
questions.solution: Plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR (which is equivalent to only 1–5% of the total incident solar radiation), and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world.

questions.question: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is always:
questions.solution: Energy flow in all ecosystems is strictly unidirectional—from the sun to producers and then to consumers. Energy is dissipated as metabolic heat at each trophic step in accordance with the Second Law of Thermodynamics and is never recycled back to the sun.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the major types of Food Chains in an ecosystem:

List-I (Food Chain Type)List-II (Starting Source & Primary Conduit)
(A) Grazing Food Chain (GFC)(I) Begins with dead organic matter/detritus; major conduit for energy flow in terrestrial ecosystems
(B) Detritus Food Chain (DFC)(II) Begins with living green photosynthetic autotrophs; major conduit for energy flow in aquatic ecosystems

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Grazing Food Chain (GFC) begins with living photosynthetic autotrophs (producers) and is the major conduit for energy flow in aquatic ecosystems. Detritus Food Chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter (detritus) and constitutes the major conduit of energy flow in terrestrial ecosystems.

questions.question: In an aquatic ecosystem (such as a pond or ocean), which food chain serves as the major conduit for energy flow?
questions.solution: In an aquatic ecosystem, the Grazing Food Chain (GFC) is the major conduit for energy flow. In a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the Detritus Food Chain (DFC) than through the GFC.

questions.question: Organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain based on the source of their nutrition or food. This position is called their:
questions.solution: Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain that is known as their trophic level. Producers belong to the first, herbivores to the second, and carnivores to subsequent trophic levels.

questions.question: According to Lindeman's 10 percent law of energy transfer, only 10 percent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level. If $20,000\text{ Joules}$ of energy is available at the producer level (first trophic level), how much energy will be available to the Tertiary Consumer (fourth trophic level)?
questions.solution: $\text{Producers } (T_1) = 20,000\text{ J} \to \text{Primary Consumers } (T_2) = 2,000\text{ J} \to \text{Secondary Consumers } (T_3) = 200\text{ J} \to \text{Tertiary Consumers } (T_4) = 20\text{ J}$.

questions.question: The standing crop of an ecosystem at a particular time is measured as the:
options: Mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area
Total amount of inorganic nutrients present in the soil
Total volume of water vapor released per year
Amount of solar radiation reflected back into space
questions.solution: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area.

questions.question: Measurement of biomass in terms of ________ is considered more accurate than ________ because it eliminates variations due to water content:
questions.solution: Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate than fresh weight because the water content of organisms fluctuates dramatically with physiological and environmental conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following ecological pyramids is ALWAYS upright and can NEVER be inverted in any ecosystem?
questions.solution: The pyramid of energy is always upright, and can never be inverted, because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step in accordance with the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

questions.question: The pyramid of biomass in a sea or lake ecosystem is generally INVERTED because:
options: The biomass of standing crop of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplankton
Phytoplankton have a very high individual weight compared to whales
Energy flow in water is bidirectional
questions.solution: The pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted because the biomass of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplankton at any given time (due to high turnover rate and rapid reproduction of microscopic phytoplanktons maintaining a small standing biomass).

questions.question: The pyramid of numbers in a single large Oak tree ecosystem supporting thousands of herbivorous insects and hyperparasites is:
questions.solution: In a tree ecosystem, a single producer (1 tree) supports a large number of herbivorous insects ($T_2$), which in turn support still larger numbers of ectoparasites and hyperparasites ($T_3, T_4$), resulting in an inverted pyramid of numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major limitation of ecological pyramids?
options: It does not accommodate a food web, assumes a simple food chain, does not consider that the same species may belong to multiple trophic levels, and gives no place to saprophytes
It cannot measure energy in Joules
It cannot be plotted for grassland ecosystems
It always assumes an inverted shape for terrestrial systems
questions.solution: Limitations of ecological pyramids: (1) It assumes a simple food chain that almost never exists in nature; it does not accommodate a food web; (2) It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels (e.g., sparrow eating seeds vs insects); (3) Saprophytes/decomposers are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

questions.question: A sparrow feeds on seeds, fruits, and peas as well as insects and worms. When eating seeds and when eating insects, the sparrow occupies which trophic levels respectively?
questions.solution: A given organism can occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously in the same ecosystem at the same time; for example, a sparrow is a primary consumer when it eats seeds, fruits, and peas, and a secondary consumer when it eats insects and worms.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding energy flow in ecosystems:
Statement I: Energy flow in an ecosystem strictly obeys the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics.
Statement II: Ecosystems need a continuous supply of energy to synthesize the molecules they require, to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness (entropy).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Living systems require a constant input of solar energy to maintain order and synthesize complex molecules, preventing entropy increase as per thermodynamic laws.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the trophic levels and representative organisms in a grassland ecosystem:

List-I (Trophic Level)List-II (Representative Organism)
(A) Fourth Trophic Level ($T_4$)(I) Grasses and Herbs
(B) Third Trophic Level ($T_3$)(II) Grasshopper (Herbivore)
(C) Second Trophic Level ($T_2$)(III) Frog / Birds (Primary carnivore)
(D) First Trophic Level ($T_1$)(IV) Vulture / Hawk (Top carnivore)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: First trophic level ($T_1$, producers): Grasses; Second trophic level ($T_2$, primary consumers): Grasshopper; Third trophic level ($T_3$, secondary consumers): Frog/birds; Fourth trophic level ($T_4$, tertiary/top consumers): Hawk/vulture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a man-made (anthropogenic) artificial ecosystem?
questions.solution: Crop fields (agroecosystems) and aquaria are man-made (artificial) ecosystems, whereas forests, grasslands, deserts, ponds, lakes, wetlands, and rivers are natural ecosystems.

questions.question: The primary producers in an aquatic ecosystem are mainly:
questions.solution: In an aquatic ecosystem, major primary producers are various species of microscopic phytoplankton, filamentous algae, and floating, submerged, or marginal macrophytes.

questions.question: Decomposers are also termed saprotrophs because they:
options: Secrete digestive enzymes outside their body onto dead organic matter and absorb the digested simpler nutrients (osmotrophy)
Engulf dead detritus by phagocytosis into food vacuoles
Synthesize food using chemical hydrogen donors
questions.solution: Decomposers (fungi and heterotrophic bacteria) are called saprotrophs (sapro: to decompose). They secrete digestive enzymes outside their body that break down dead and waste materials into simple, inorganic materials, which are then absorbed by them.

questions.question: Primary productivity depends on which of the following factors?
options: Plant species inhabiting a particular area, environmental factors (light, temp), nutrient availability, and photosynthetic capacity of plants
Number of carnivores in the top trophic level only
questions.solution: Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients, and photosynthetic capacity of plants.

questions.question: In a pond ecosystem, which autotrophic organisms constitute the primary producers?
options: Phytoplankton, some algae, and the floating, submerged, and marginal plants
questions.solution: In a small pond ecosystem, autotrophic components include phytoplankton, filamentous green algae, and floating, submerged, and marginal macrophytes found at the edges.

questions.question: In a food web, interconnected food chains prevent the extinction of a species because:
options: Alternative feeding pathways provide stability and alternate food choices if one prey species declines
Decomposers are eliminated from the system
questions.solution: In natural communities, food chains are interlinked into complex food webs. This provides alternative foraging channels, dampening population fluctuations and increasing community stability.

questions.question: An inverted pyramid of numbers is typically observed in which of the following ecosystems?
options: A single tree supporting herbivorous birds and parasites
A vast grassland with zebras and lions
A pond with phytoplankton and zooplankton
A desert ecosystem with cacti and rodents
questions.solution: In a parasite food chain on a single tree, the base is narrow (1 tree) and supports numerous birds/insects, which support thousands of hyperparasites, forming an inverted pyramid of numbers.

questions.question: If an ecosystem receives $1,000,000\text{ Joules}$ of total incident solar radiation, how much energy will be converted into net chemical energy in the primary producers, assuming $1\%$ of incident radiation is fixed into GPP and $20\%$ of GPP is lost in respiration ($R$)?
questions.solution: Incident radiation $= 1,000,000\text{ J}$. $\text{GPP} = 1\% \text{ of } 1,000,000\text{ J} = 10,000\text{ J}$. Respiration loss $R = 20\% \text{ of } 10,000\text{ J} = 2,000\text{ J}$. $\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R = 10,000 - 2,000 = 8,000\text{ Joules}$.

questions.question: The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in units of:
questions.solution: Productivity is the rate of biomass production per unit area over a time period. It is expressed in terms of weight as $\text{g}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\cdot\text{yr}^{-1}$ (or $(\text{g}/\text{m}^2)/\text{yr}$) or in terms of energy as $\text{kcal}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\cdot\text{yr}^{-1}$ (or $(\text{kcal}/\text{m}^2)/\text{yr}$).

questions.question: Which of the following organisms in an ecosystem are responsible for initiating the Detritus Food Chain (DFC)?
questions.solution: The Detritus Food Chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter (detritus). It is made up of decomposers which are heterotrophic organisms, mainly fungi and bacteria.

questions.question: What happens to the amount of available energy at successive higher trophic levels in an ecosystem?
options: It decreases progressively due to respiratory loss and incomplete assimilation
It remains constant at all trophic levels
It fluctuates randomly without any rule
questions.solution: Energy decreases at each successive higher trophic level because only about 10% of the energy is conserved and stored in biomass at each level; the remaining 90% is lost during respiration and heat dissipation.

questions.question: In a terrestrial grassland ecosystem, the pyramid of numbers and pyramid of biomass are:
options: Pyramid of numbers is inverted and pyramid of biomass is upright
Pyramid of numbers is upright and pyramid of biomass is inverted
questions.solution: In a grassland ecosystem, producers (grasses) are maximum in numbers and possess maximum total biomass. Primary consumers (grasshoppers) and secondary consumers (frogs, snakes) have progressively smaller numbers and biomass. Hence, both pyramids are upright.

questions.question: Debris such as dead plant remains (leaves, bark, flowers) and dead remains of animals, including fecal matter, constitute the raw material for decomposition called:
questions.solution: Dead plant remains such as leaves, bark, flowers and dead remains of animals, including fecal matter, constitute detritus, which is the raw material for decomposition.

questions.question: Why are top carnivores (such as lions, tigers, and eagles) always small in number in any natural ecological pyramid of numbers?
options: Because very little energy is available at the fourth or fifth trophic level to support a large population
Because top carnivores have very short lifespans
Because top carnivores eat plants exclusively during winter
Because decomposers destroy top carnivores before maturity
questions.solution: Because of the 10% law of energy transfer, only a tiny fraction of the original solar energy reaches the highest trophic levels. Consequently, top carnivores must have large hunting territories and can only be supported in small numbers.

questions.question: The term 'Biomass' of a trophic level refers to the:
options: Total dry or fresh weight of all living organisms present in a unit area at a given time
Total amount of carbon dioxide gas fixed per year
Total volume of dead detritus floating in water
Sum total of inorganic salts dissolved in groundwater
questions.solution: Biomass is the total mass of living biological organisms in a given area or ecosystem at a given time, expressed as fresh weight or dry weight.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: A single species can never occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem.
Statement II: In nature, saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids.

Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution: Statement I is incorrect because a species can occupy multiple trophic levels simultaneously depending on diet (e.g., humans or sparrows). Statement II is correct because saprophytes are excluded from ecological pyramids despite their vital ecological role.

questions.question: In a forest ecosystem, which of the following represents the primary consumers ($T_2$)?
questions.solution: In a forest ecosystem, primary consumers ($T_2$) are herbivores that feed directly on primary producers, such as deer, elephants, monkeys, and fruit-eating birds.

questions.question: The breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by earthworms is specifically called:
questions.solution: Detritivores (such as earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles. This physical breakdown process is called fragmentation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding ecological pyramids is INCORRECT?
options: Pyramid of energy can sometimes be inverted in marine ecosystems.
Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted.
Pyramid of numbers in a grassland is upright.
Pyramid of biomass in a forest is upright.
questions.solution: Pyramid of energy is ALWAYS upright and can NEVER be inverted under any circumstances because energy is dissipated as heat at every trophic transfer step.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Net primary productivity (NPP) is the available biomass for consumption by heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).
Statement II: In aquatic ecosystems, grazing food chain (GFC) is the major conduit for energy flow.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Net primary productivity (NPP) represents the net plant biomass remaining after respiratory utilization, which is available to herbivores and decomposers. In aquatic ecosystems, GFC is the primary pathway of energy flow.
